messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The issue report states that in the method WordUtils.abbreviate, the parameters controlling substring limits are mishandled when the 'lower' bound is larger than the string length. Examining the code:

- The method receives the input string `str`, and two bounds `lower` and `upper`, plus an optional string `appendToEnd`.
- It correctly adjusts `upper` when it's -1 or greater than `str.length()` by setting `upper` to `str.length()` (lines 618-619).
- It then raises `upper` to `lower` if `upper < lower` (lines 621-623).
- However, there is no similar adjustment for `lower` if it exceeds `str.length()`. This means `lower` can remain greater than string length.
- Later in the code, the method calls `StringUtils.indexOf(str, " ", lower)`. If `lower > str.length()`, this likely passes an out-of-bounds index.
- More critically, if no space is found after `lower`, the method appends `str.substring(0, upper)` (line 629). If `upper` has been adjusted to `lower` which is greater than `str.length()`, `str.substring(0, upper)` will throw a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException.
- The test that failed has a call where `lower` is 15 and `upper` is 20 while the string length is 10, leading `upper` to be set to 20 then adjusted to 20 (from 15), but `str.substring(0, upper)` tries to access beyond string length.

The root cause is the missing adjustment of `lower` to be at most the string length, which leads to `upper` also being out of bounds and subsequent substring exceptions.

The fix should be to clamp `lower` to `str.length()` early on, just as it is done for `upper`.

Recent bug reports are unrelated; they focus on unrelated parts of the codebase.

This diagnosis matches the failure observed in the test `WordUtilsTest.testAbbreviate`.

Next, I will identify the suitable method(s) to fix this bug.
org.apache.commons.lang.WordUtils.abbreviate(java.lang.String,int,int,java.lang.String)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
